ann_44.original: board_weighting: a linear positional-value map over 29 squares (x = +1, o = -1, z-scored), read straight into the output logit. Hypothesis: a piece is worth more to its owner the more four-in-a-row lines pass through its square, as in the classic line-count heuristic (3 4 5 7 5 4 3 / 4 6 8 10 8 6 4 / 5 8 11 13 11 8 5 for rows 1-3, mirrored above). Evidence (train, 54,045 positions): per-square effects of the whole network (x or o instead of empty) peak at d3 (+2.83 / -2.83), then c3, d2, d4, e3; edge columns a and g count slightly against their owner (-0.2..-0.3); rarely occupied top squares (b6, f6, g6) count strongly against their owner. Correlation with the line counts over the 32 squares occupied in >1% of positions: 0.88 (x) and 0.86 (o). The board weighting correlates 0.88 with line-count-weighted material (x minus o), which alone reaches AUC 0.82; the network logit is 82% explained by that one feature. Mean-ablating this leaf drops train AUC from 0.856 to 0.493. Exceptions: the map is static, so it does not see threats (r = 0.07 with three-in-a-line counts; in the 765 positions where o has a three-with-an-empty-square, x wins 26% but the network predicts 49% on average) or open two-in-a-rows (the largest residual signal, r = 0.13). A 12-feature domain logistic regression (line material, centre, edges, open lines, open twos, threats) reaches AUC 0.868, above the network.
ann_44.proposed: One value per square for 29 squares, highest on the low central squares (c3, d2, c2, d1, d3) and negative for its owner on high squares such as g6 and b6.

ann_45.original: f1_asymmetry: hinge on square f1 (bottom of column f), weight 0.303 to the output. Logit contribution 0 with o on f1, +0.12 empty, +0.57 with x on f1: relative to empty, x on f1 +0.46, o on f1 only -0.12, i.e. the o penalty is cut off. Evidence: full-train line plot (exit vs z(f1), corr 0.92); restore gain +0.0005 AUC (the largest non-linear gain in the network); mean ablation AUC 0.853. Ground truth: an unconstrained one-hot regression gives +0.21 for both x and o on f1 (an occupied f1 helps x whoever owns it), so the hinge moves in the direction of the data, but no domain concept (lines through f1: 4, threats, row parity) predicts this asymmetry. It is a per-square correction of the symmetric x/o coding, not a domain feature.
ann_45.proposed: An x on the bottom square f1 raises the predicted chance that x wins more than an o there lowers it.

ann_46.original: c5_negligible: hinge on square c5 with output weight 0.047: x on c5 +0.075, o on c5 -0.019 logit vs empty. Support-level near-null: mean ablation changes AUC by 1e-5 and p by at most 0.018; restore gain -0.00002. Its sign for x on c5 disagrees with the one-hot regression (-0.13). No domain reading.
ann_46.proposed: Square c5 barely changes the predictions.

ann_47.original: e4_f3_pair: hinge 1722 = relu(1.2 + 0.345 z(e4) + 0.43 z(f3)) on two squares of the same down-right diagonal, passed on linearly by 611_a (always on) with weight 1.305 to the output (and through 611_b into the f6 unit, a further -0.032). Logit contribution: 2.73 both empty (46,617 positions), 4.14 x on e4, 3.69 x on f3, floor 1.87 with o on e4 or on f3. Domain reading of the values: e4 (11 lines) and f3 (8 lines) are part of the positional map: x there helps x (+1.37, +0.92), o there hurts (-0.83 each); these agree with a one-hot regression (+1.20/-0.83, +0.50/-0.65). The non-linear part (the o penalty is capped, joint e4/f3 'diagonal' behaviour) has no support: only 18 positions have both squares occupied, and replacing the leaf with its best linear fit raises AUC by 0.00018 (restore gain -0.00018). So: two more squares of the board weighting, routed through a hinge that does nothing useful.
ann_47.proposed: Squares e4 and f3 count for their owner: an x there raises the predicted chance that x wins, an o there lowers it.

ann_48.original: f6_top_square: unit 5461 = relu(0.626 + 1.27 z(f6) + 0.341 * 611_b), output weight -0.095. f6 is the top square of column f: x is on it in 16 training positions, o in 59. Logit contribution -0.13 empty, 0 with o on f6 (unit off), -3.34 with x on f6. Otherwise (611_b is always on) it is a near-linear -0.032 rescale of the e4/f3 signal. Ground truth: x on f6 positions have x win rate 0.31 (network 0.22), o on f6 0.81 (network 0.75); stacking three x pieces in column f without x on top (420 positions) has win rate 0.72, so the effect is not 'x has wasted pieces in column f'. It is a large weight fitted to 16 rare positions (z(f6) is huge because x on f6 is so rare). Restore gain +0.00006 AUC; mean ablation AUC 0.8557.
ann_48.proposed: An x on the top square f6 lowers the predicted chance that x wins a lot; an o there changes nothing.

ann_49.original: e4_f3_with_f6: serial composition of e4_f3_pair and f6_top_square through the relay edge 1722 -> 611_b. Because 611 is on in every training position and 5461 in all but 59, the f6 path only rescales the e4/f3 signal (-0.095 * 0.341 = -0.032 per unit of 611) and adds the f6 effect, so the two children combine additively in logit: contribution = 1.273 * relu(1.43 + 0.553 * e4f3_hinge) - 0.095 * (0.626 + 1.27 z(f6)) on almost all positions.
ann_49.proposed: Squares e4 and f3 count for their owner; an x on the top square f6 lowers the predicted chance that x wins a lot, an o there does not change it.

ann_50.original: position_value: P(x wins) = sigmoid(-1.78 + board_weighting + 0.303 f1_asymmetry + 0.047 c5_negligible + 1.305 e4_f3_pair[611_a] - 0.095 f6_top_square). All children add in logit. The network is essentially a linear positional-value evaluation: a weighted count of x's minus o's pieces in which central low squares (column d, rows 2-4; then c and e) are worth most, close to the classic count of winning lines through each square (network logit correlates 0.91 with line-count-weighted material). Squares c6, d6, e5, e6, f5, g4, a5, a6 are unconnected (zero-effect entries). The non-linear units are single- or two-square corrections: replacing all four by their best linear fit lowers train AUC only from 0.8559 to 0.8555 (restore gain 0.0004 in total), consistent with logistic regression (0.857). It does not see threats, zugzwang or row parity: where o already has three in a line with an empty fourth square (765 positions) x wins 26% but the network predicts 49%. Adding simple domain features (open lines, open twos, threats) to the network logit lifts AUC to 0.880 and gradient boosting reaches 0.947, so most of the game-theoretic structure is not represented.
ann_50.proposed: The model gives every square a value and adds them up: a piece on a low central square, above all c3, d2, c2 and d1, counts for its owner, a piece on a high square counts against its owner, and eight mostly top-row squares are ignored.

parts.name: board_weighting
parts.original_hypothesis: board_weighting: a linear positional-value map over 29 squares (x = +1, o = -1, z-scored), read straight into the output logit. Hypothesis: a piece is worth more to its owner the more four-in-a-row lines pass through its square, as in the classic line-count heuristic (3 4 5 7 5 4 3 / 4 6 8 10 8 6 4 / 5 8 11 13 11 8 5 for rows 1-3, mirrored above). Evidence (train, 54,045 positions): per-square effects of the whole network (x or o instead of empty) peak at d3 (+2.83 / -2.83), then c3, d2, d4, e3; edge columns a and g count slightly against their owner (-0.2..-0.3); rarely occupied top squares (b6, f6, g6) count strongly against their owner. Correlation with the line counts over the 32 squares occupied in >1% of positions: 0.88 (x) and 0.86 (o). The board weighting correlates 0.88 with line-count-weighted material (x minus o), which alone reaches AUC 0.82; the network logit is 82% explained by that one feature. Mean-ablating this leaf drops train AUC from 0.856 to 0.493. Exceptions: the map is static, so it does not see threats (r = 0.07 with three-in-a-line counts; in the 765 positions where o has a three-with-an-empty-square, x wins 26% but the network predicts 49% on average) or open two-in-a-rows (the largest residual signal, r = 0.13). A 12-feature domain logistic regression (line material, centre, edges, open lines, open twos, threats) reaches AUC 0.868, above the network.
